concept.name: Demand zone
concept.definition: A price band marking the base from which a strong advance launched, drawn (in supply-and-demand methodology) around the small consolidation preceding the impulsive rally. It is treated as potential support on a return, on the hypothesis that unfilled buy interest remains there — a discretionary zone framework related to, but looser than, classical support.
concept.intuition: Price paused, then took off upward; the pause zone is where buyers were last in control, so the first return there may attract them again.
concept.mechanics: Identify an impulsive rally; step back to the small base candles just before it and box the base (proximal edge nearest current price, distal edge at the base extreme). Reversal zones (drop-base-rally) form at swing lows; continuation zones (rally-base-rally) form mid-swing and are regarded by practitioners as weaker.
concept.failure_modes: Zone boundaries are subjective and hindsight-fitted; price frequently slices through demand zones without reacting, especially continuation-type zones formed mid-swing.
concept.misconceptions: That an untouched ('fresh') demand zone must hold on first test; freshness heuristics are practitioner rules of thumb without validated statistics.
concept.example: GBP/JPY bases at 182.00-182.30, then rallies sharply; the base is drawn as a demand zone, and a later retracement into it produces a bullish engulfing entry.
